title: Uncertain failure curves: scenarios and what changes

questions.heading: The Design Decision: A Plan per Scenario, an Expected-Value Plan, or a Worst-Case Plan
questions.stem: A planner wants the plan whose least favorable scenario removes the most risk. What does that objective add to the model?

options.text: Nothing new, since a weighted mean of scenarios is still linear
options.says: That is the expected-value objective; a minimum is not a mean.

options.text: One variable, and a row per scenario that it must stay below
options.says: Right: max z with z at most each scenario's value.

options.text: A second stage of decisions, made once the curves are known
options.says: The curves are not revealed during the plan, so there is no second stage.

options.text: One plan per scenario, solved one after another and merged
options.says: Per-scenario plans are a separate study; the worst case is one model.

questions.heading: The Plans Differ in Timing, Hardly in Value
questions.stem: Every plan is solved to a 0.5% gap. Under one scenario, plan P removes $20,000k less than plan Q, out of about $7,000,000k. What does the lesson conclude from numbers like these?

options.text: P is worse, since its regret is above Q's despite the gap
options.says: A shortfall of about 0.3% is inside the 0.5% gap: not evidence.

options.text: Q is the best plan, since the gap bounds only P's search
options.says: Q was found by a search that may also have stopped up to 0.5% short.

options.text: The solver failed, since a gap cannot give a negative regret
options.says: The table shows a negative regret, which stopped searches can give.

options.text: Nothing about which is better, since it is inside the gap
options.says: Right: differences inside the gap are not evidence.

questions.heading: Design Note: Value Plans Outside the Model
questions.stem: To compare the expected-value plan with the worst-case plan, why does the lesson use `evaluate` instead of each solve's objective value?

options.text: The objectives measure different things, at different gaps
options.says: Right: a mean, a minimum, one scenario; a plan's value is one sum.

options.text: The worst-case solve reports no objective, only a plan
The expected objective is in $k, the worst case in units
options.says: Both objectives are risk removed in $k.

options.text: The objectives are exact, while `evaluate` rounds to $k
options.says: `evaluate` is exact arithmetic over the plan's coefficients.
